Runs Freenet v%2$s on your phone. This is an unofficial build, not made by The Freenet Project.

About the project

Freenet is a decentralised network: there is no central server, and every node both uses the network and carries other people\'s traffic. This app packs a real Freenet node into an Android app, so a phone becomes one of those nodes, with no PC needed.

What it does:

  • Starts and stops the node as a foreground service, and shows how many peers it is connected to.
  • Opens the node\'s web interface inside the app, so Freenet apps and pages work on the phone.
  • Builds and publishes a website from the phone, with an HTML, CSS and JavaScript editor, or by importing a folder.
  • Keeps the site files and their keys encrypted on the phone.
  • Joins the Room chat, asking for an invite by itself.
  • Can serve the node to a PC, over USB or over the local network.
  • Checks GitHub for new versions and verifies what it downloads before installing.

Telemetry and the node\'s own automatic updates are turned off. The web interface can only be reached from this phone, unless you turn on host mode in the settings.

Sends the app\'s own requests (update check, chat invite, gateway list) through Orbot on this phone. Orbot must be installed and running. It does not cover the Freenet node, which uses UDP: Tor cannot carry it.
Tor on for the app\'s requests. Start Orbot, or they will fail.
Lets a PC on the same Wi-Fi use this phone as the Freenet server. Without it, only the USB cable works.

The node has no password. With host mode on, anyone on the same Wi-Fi can open your node, read your data and use your keys. Only turn it on on a network you trust, and turn it off afterwards.\n\nThere is no public internet address: that would need a port opened on your router, and the node would then be open to everyone.
